name: Ketone ester (beta-hydroxybutyrate ester) supplement
short: ALS trial (81 people, 6 months): function declined faster on the ester than on placebo in the unadjusted analysis (not after adjustment); adverse events similar. Single doses lowered blood glucose.
text: In a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 2 trial in 81 people with ALS, a D-beta-hydroxybutyrate ester taken by mouth for 6 months was well tolerated, with a similar frequency of adverse events in both groups; however, in the unadjusted analysis the ALS functional rating score declined faster in the ester group than with placebo, while the adjusted analysis found no significant difference in clinical endpoints. In short studies of a ketone monoester drink, no adverse effects were observed after a single dose before a meal in 10 adults with type 2 diabetes, in whom it lowered blood glucose after the meal by about 18% at 2 hours; in 14 healthy young adults, tolerability of single doses was similar to a monoester and salt mixture, and aftertaste was reported more often with the monoester. In a study of 10 people (5 with alcohol use disorder and 5 healthy controls), a single dose of a ketone ester also lowered blood glucose. The abstract of the alcohol use disorder study does not report adverse events or whether the fall in blood glucose caused symptoms. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
